title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in 'Analysis situs (deuxième mouture)' (June 1986) Grothendieck is building an axiomatic, essentially point-free framework for tame ('modérée') topology. He works with a structure M of objects called multistructures (X, Y, ...). These carry an inclusion-like relation ≪ ('X' is a piece/fragment of X') and a disjointness relation ∥ (also written as a cross over M, opposed to the set-theoretic disjointness written with 'ens'). From these he forms 'atlases' 𝔉 (families F, G, ... of such objects) subject to axioms At 1, At 2, ..., At 8 (At 8 was called the 'axiome des lieux'?).

On this page he turns to axioms of disjointness.

(1) Definition. For F, G in 𝔉 (inside T), F ∥ G iff every X in F̃ is disjoint from every Y in G̃. F̃ is presumably the set of members, or of refinements, of F.

(2) Proposition. For an atlas satisfying At 1–At 3 (without using ≪), the definition behaves well; he marks this 'immédiat'.

(3) Corollary (1.58), which is the property one 'would like'. If F ∥ G, F' ≪ F and G' ≪ G, then F' ∥ G'. That is, disjointness is hereditary (downward closed) in each variable.

(4) Proof sketch. By the proposition one reduces to F' = X', G' = Y'. One then reduces to F = X, G = Y, and the statement for single objects is supplied by an axiom At 9.

(5) Self-critique. In the set-theoretic model, the hereditary property for the geometric relation does not seem to follow from the other axioms. He refers to p. 55, where At 7 (and 3 or 8?) only impose two conditions on the relation ∥_M:
- it is stable under some passage to (strict) sums or limits;
- it is stronger than set-theoretic disjointness.

The next page gives a counterexample. With reduced multistructures given by sets A, B, A' (A' ⊄ A, A ∩ B = ∅), one may choose ∥_M arbitrarily on the pairs, making X ∥ Y but not X' ∥ Y even though X' ≪ X. So hereditariness must be imposed as a new axiom (*): X' ≪ X, Y' ≪ Y, X ∥ Y ⇒ X' ∥ Y'.

Margin notes:
- Top: X ∥ Y should imply that the underlying supports S(X), S(Y) have empty intersection, 'a fortiori' in the set-theoretic sense.
- Bottom: 'the only problem' is proving the passage from F ∥ G to F' ∥ G'. He considers Z ≪ F, Z ≪ G ⇒ Z ≪ F ∪ G-type arguments and asks whether this is immediate.

Mathematically this is the standard step of making a 'non-overlap' relation monotone, as in contact/proximity algebras or orthogonality relations on posets.
errors: The corollary's proof as first written relies on 'At 9', which had not yet been established as following from the other axioms. Grothendieck himself notices this: in the set-theoretic model it does not follow from At 7 and At 3 (or 8). Page 60 confirms it with a counterexample, so heredity must be added as an independent axiom (*). This is a gap that he self-corrects, not an error in the final text.

ideas.what: Extending a disjointness relation from single objects to atlases/families: F ∥ G iff all members are pairwise disjoint
ideas.modern_name: Disjointness/orthogonality of families; lifting a binary relation to subsets (∀∀-lifting)

ideas.what: Hereditary (downward-closed) disjointness axiom: X' ≪ X, Y' ≪ Y, X ∥ Y ⇒ X' ∥ Y'
ideas.modern_name: Monotonicity of the contact relation (its complement, 'non-contact', is downward closed) in contact/proximity algebras and mereotopology
ideas.usually_credited_to: de Vries (1962) compingent algebras; Dimov–Vakarelov contact algebras (2000s); Whiteheadian mereotopology

ideas.what: Observation that a geometric disjointness relation need only be stronger than set-theoretic disjointness, so heredity is not automatic and must be imposed
ideas.modern_name: Independence of an axiom, shown by a set-theoretic countermodel

missed.claim: The 1986 Analysis situs axiomatics treats 'multistructures' with a containment relation ≪ and a separately axiomatized disjointness relation that is stronger than set-theoretic disjointness. This is close in spirit to contact algebras / mereotopology and to the point-free topology of 'regions'. These were later developed independently, and no literature links Grothendieck's tame-topology programme to them.
missed.quote: la relation ×_M : d'être stable par limites [sommes?] croissantes strictes, et d'être plus forte que la relation ×_ens
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is only of historical interest: it shows Grothendieck's 'topologie modérée' was being formalized as a region-based (mereotopological) axiom system, not via o-minimal structures. The page itself contains no nontrivial result.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine axiomatics step: a definition lifted to families, a monotonicity corollary, and the realization that the monotonicity needs its own axiom. It is mildly interesting only as evidence of the style of the unpublished 1986 Analysis situs axiomatics.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: the quoted axiom name for At 8 is not clearly 'lieux'. It reads more like 'l'"axiome des b..x"' and is uncertain.
Bottom line: 'stable [?] par limites [?] croissantes [?] strictes' more plausibly reads 'stable par passage aux sommes strictes' (the word 'croissantes' is doubtful).
'(on n'a pas [?] utiliser ≪)' likely reads '(on n'a pas à utiliser ≪)'.
The insertion above the proof is '(par prop.)'; the struck-out 'Proposition' before (1.58) is replaced by 'Corollaire'.

The top-left margin seems to read roughly 'Remarque pour X∥Y ⟹ ... ∅ = S(X) ∩ S(Y) ... a fortiori ...'. It concerns the supports being disjoint, and the transcription's duplicated '0 = S(X) ∩ 0 = S(Y)' is a misreading.
